1	# Phase 30 — Procedural Skills
2	
3	> Date: 2026-03-26
4	> Status: Planned
5	> Phase: 30
6	> Depends on: Phase 26b (Candle LLM), Phase 15a (causal schemas), Phase 11 (HTN)
7	> Enhances: Phase 29b (skill exposure), Phase 31 (skill intelligence)
8	> ADR: [040-procedural-skills](../decisions/040-procedural-skills.md)
9	
10	## Motivation
11	
12	Akh-medu skills currently carry facts and inference rules but no procedural
13	knowledge — "how to do things." A human expects a "skill" to mean capability:
14	"I know how to review code", not just "I know facts about code review."
15	
16	The engine already has procedural representation mechanisms (HTN, causal schemas,
17	MCTS, event calculus) but they're disconnected from the skill system. And the
18	formal syntax for egg rules is a barrier for most users.
19	
20	This phase bridges both gaps: extend skills with procedural knowledge, and use
21	the LLM to make skill authoring accessible.
22	
23	## Sub-phases
24	
25	### 30a — Extended Skill Format (~400 lines)
26	
27	Add `actions.json` and `plans.json` to the skill directory structure.
28	
29	**Extend SkillManifest**:
30	```rust
31	pub struct SkillManifest {
32	    // ... existing fields ...
33	    pub actions_file: Option<String>,    // Path to actions.json (default: "actions.json")
34	    pub plans_file: Option<String>,      // Path to plans.json (default: "plans.json")
35	    pub procedures_file: Option<String>, // Path to procedures.md (source of truth)
36	}
37	```
38	
39	**ActionSchema** (reuse existing `src/agent/causal.rs` types):
40	```rust
41	// actions.json is deserialized into Vec<SkillAction>
42	pub struct SkillAction {
43	    pub action: String,              // Action name (becomes a SymbolId)
44	    pub description: String,         // Human-readable purpose
45	    pub preconditions: Vec<String>,  // Fluent names that must hold
46	    pub effects: SkillEffects,
47	    pub estimated_duration: Option<String>, // "fast", "medium", "slow"
48	}
49	
50	pub struct SkillEffects {
51	    pub initiates: Vec<String>,      // Fluents this action starts
52	    pub terminates: Vec<String>,     // Fluents this action ends
53	}
54	```
55	
56	**PlanTemplate** (maps to HTN decomposition):
57	```rust
58	// plans.json is deserialized into Vec<SkillPlan>
59	pub struct SkillPlan {
60	    pub goal: String,                // Goal name (becomes a SymbolId)
61	    pub method: PlanMethod,          // How steps are organized
62	    pub steps: Vec<String>,          // Action names (references to actions.json)
63	    pub preconditions: Vec<String>,  // When this plan is applicable
64	    pub alternatives: Vec<String>,   // Other plan names that achieve the same goal
65	}
66	
67	pub enum PlanMethod {
68	    Sequential,                      // Steps must execute in order
69	    Parallel,                        // Steps can execute concurrently
70	    Conditional(Vec<ConditionalStep>), // Steps depend on runtime conditions
71	}
72	
73	pub struct ConditionalStep {
74	    pub condition: String,           // Fluent to check
75	    pub then_step: String,           // Action if true
76	    pub else_step: Option<String>,   // Action if false
77	}
78	```
79	
80	**Modify**: `src/skills/mod.rs`, `src/skills/manager.rs`
81	
82	### 30b — Activation Wiring (~500 lines)
83	
84	Wire skill activation to the procedural reasoning systems.
85	
86	**On skill activate (Hot)**:
87	```rust
88	// In SkillManager::activate() — after triples + rules:
89	
90	// 1. Load action schemas → CausalManager
91	if let Some(actions_path) = manifest.actions_file {
92	    let actions: Vec<SkillAction> = load_json(&skill_dir.join(actions_path))?;
93	    for action in &actions {
94	        let schema = action.to_causal_schema(engine)?; // resolve labels to SymbolIds
95	        engine.causal_manager().register_action_schema(schema)?;
96	    }
97	}
98	
99	// 2. Load plan templates → HTN decomposer + MCTS seed
100	if let Some(plans_path) = manifest.plans_file {
101	    let plans: Vec<SkillPlan> = load_json(&skill_dir.join(plans_path))?;
102	    for plan in &plans {
103	        let htn_rule = plan.to_htn_rule(engine)?;
104	        engine.htn_decomposer().register_rule(htn_rule)?;
105	
106	        // Seed MCTS with known-good plans for warm-start
107	        let mcts_seed = plan.to_mcts_seed(engine)?;
108	        engine.mcts_planner().add_seed(mcts_seed)?;
109	    }
110	}
111	```
112	
113	**On skill deactivate (Warm)**:
114	- Deregister action schemas from CausalManager (by skill_id tag)
115	- Remove HTN rules from decomposer (by skill_id tag)
116	- Remove MCTS seeds (by skill_id tag)
117	
118	**Provenance**: All skill-originated actions/plans get
119	`DerivationKind::SkillProcedure { skill_id, source_file }` provenance.
120	
121	**Modify**: `src/skills/manager.rs`, `src/agent/causal.rs`, `src/agent/ooda.rs`
122	
123	### 30c — LLM-Assisted Skill Authoring (~800 lines)
124	
125	**New module**: `src/skills/author.rs`
126	
127	The authoring pipeline takes natural language and produces a complete skill:
128	
129	```rust
130	pub struct SkillAuthor {
131	    llm: Arc<CandleBackend>,     // Phase 26b
132	    grammar: Arc<ConcreteGrammar>,
133	    engine: Arc<Engine>,
134	}
135	
136	pub struct AuthoredSkill {
137	    pub manifest: SkillManifest,
138	    pub triples: Vec<LabelTriple>,
139	    pub actions: Vec<SkillAction>,
140	    pub plans: Vec<SkillPlan>,
141	    pub rules: Vec<String>,          // egg rule strings
142	    pub source_text: String,         // Original natural language
143	}
144	
145	impl SkillAuthor {
146	    /// Generate a complete skill from natural language description
147	    pub fn author_from_description(
148	        &self,
149	        name: &str,
150	        description: &str,
151	        domains: &[String],
152	    ) -> SkillResult<AuthoredSkill>;
153	
154	    /// Re-generate structured files from updated procedures.md
155	    pub fn regenerate_from_procedures(
156	        &self,
157	        skill_id: &str,
158	        procedures_text: &str,
159	    ) -> SkillResult<AuthoredSkill>;
160	}
161	```
162	
163	**LLM prompt strategy** (structured extraction):
164	
165	The LLM receives a system prompt with:
166	1. The skill format specification (JSON schemas for actions/plans)
167	2. Examples of well-formed skills
168	3. The user's natural language description
169	
170	Output is constrained to produce valid JSON sections via the LogitsProcessor
171	(Phase 26b) or brace-depth tracking.
172	
173	**Multi-pass extraction**:
174	1. **Concept pass**: Extract domain entities and relationships → triples
175	2. **Action pass**: Extract steps with preconditions/effects → actions
176	3. **Plan pass**: Extract goal decomposition and ordering → plans
177	4. **Rule pass**: Extract heuristics and inference patterns → rules
178	5. **Validation pass**: Check internal consistency (all action refs in plans
179	   exist, all preconditions reference known fluents)
180	
181	Each pass uses a focused prompt to avoid overwhelming the small LLM.
182	For Qwen2.5-1.5B, this means 5 short inference calls rather than 1 long one.
183	
184	**NLU integration**:
185	- New dialogue act: `SkillTeach { name, description }`
186	- Grammar patterns: "teach me to...", "learn how to...", "I want to show you how..."
187	- ChatProcessor routes to SkillAuthor when detected
188	
189	### 30d — Rule Refinement Loop (~600 lines)
190	
191	**New module**: `src/skills/refine.rs`
192	
193	When the agent executes a skill's procedures and encounters problems:
194	
195	```rust
196	pub struct SkillRefiner {
197	    llm: Arc<CandleBackend>,
198	    engine: Arc<Engine>,
199	}
200	
201	pub struct RefinementSuggestion {
202	    pub skill_id: String,
203	    pub kind: RefinementKind,
204	    pub description: String,         // Human-readable explanation
205	    pub confidence: f32,
206	    pub source_failure: ProvenanceId, // What provoked this suggestion
207	}
208	
209	pub enum RefinementKind {
210	    NewRule { lhs: String, rhs: String },
211	    ModifiedPrecondition { action: String, add: Vec<String>, remove: Vec<String> },
212	    AlternativePlan { goal: String, new_method: SkillPlan },
213	    NewAction { action: SkillAction },
214	    TripleMissing { triple: LabelTriple },
215	}
216	```
217	
218	**Failure analysis pipeline**:
219	1. Agent executes plan from skill, action fails (precondition unmet or
220	   unexpected outcome)
221	2. Engine records failure with full provenance chain
222	3. Refiner queries: "What state was expected? What state was actual?
223	   What inference path was taken?"
224	4. LLM receives the failure context + skill's procedures.md
225	5. LLM generates RefinementSuggestions
226	6. Suggestions stored as pending (KG triples with `skill:pending_refinement`
227	   predicate)
228	7. User reviews via MCP/CLI/dashboard: approve, reject, or modify
229	
230	**Idle task integration**:
231	- New daemon idle task: `refine_skills` (runs every 30 min)
232	- Scans recent failures involving skill procedures
233	- Batches failure contexts for efficient LLM processing
234	- Accumulates suggestions without blocking
235	
236	### 30e — Skill Quality Metrics (~300 lines)
237	
238	**New module**: `src/skills/quality.rs`
239	
240	Track per-skill effectiveness:
241	
242	```rust
243	pub struct SkillQuality {
244	    pub skill_id: String,
245	    pub success_rate: f32,           // Plans completed / plans attempted
246	    pub failure_modes: Vec<FailureMode>,
247	    pub rule_hit_rates: HashMap<String, f32>, // Rule name → % of inferences it participated in
248	    pub triple_coverage: f32,        // % of triples ever queried
249	    pub last_used: Option<u64>,      // Timestamp
250	    pub total_uses: u32,
251	    pub refinements_applied: u32,
252	    pub refinements_pending: u32,
253	}
254	
255	pub struct FailureMode {
256	    pub action: String,
257	    pub failure_type: String,        // "precondition_unmet", "unexpected_effect", "timeout"
258	    pub count: u32,
259	    pub last_occurrence: u64,
260	}
261	```
262	
263	**Storage**: Quality metrics stored as KG triples with `skill:quality_*`
264	predicates. Updated after each plan execution involving the skill.
265	
266	**Staleness detection**: If a skill hasn't been used in N days and has low
267	coverage, suggest deactivation to free memory budget.
268	
269	**MCP tools**: `skill_quality(skill_id)` returns the metrics.
270	**Dashboard**: Quality panel in Phase 29b skill browser.
271	
272	## Estimated Effort
273	
274	| Sub-phase | Lines | Complexity | Dependencies |
275	|---|---|---|---|
276	| 30a — Extended format | ~400 | Low | None (schema only) |
277	| 30b — Activation wiring | ~500 | Medium | Phase 15a, 11, 16 |
278	| 30c — LLM authoring | ~800 | High | Phase 26b (Candle) |
279	| 30d — Rule refinement | ~600 | High | Phase 26b, 30b |
280	| 30e — Quality metrics | ~300 | Low | 30b |
281	| **Total** | **~2,600** | | |
282	
283	## New Dependencies
284	
285	None — uses existing Candle (Phase 26b), serde for JSON, and existing engine
286	subsystems (CausalManager, HTN, MCTS).
287	
288	## Feature Flags
289	
290	```toml
291	[features]
292	skill-author = ["candle-backend"]  # LLM-assisted authoring (30c, 30d)
293	# 30a, 30b, 30e have no additional feature requirements
294	```

296	## Example: Teaching a Skill via Natural Language
297	
298	```
299	User: "I want to teach you how to triage a bug report"
300	
301	Agent: "I'll create a skill for that. Please describe the procedure."
302	
303	User: "First categorize the bug: crash, incorrect behavior, or cosmetic.
304	       Then assess severity based on impact — crashes are always critical.
305	       For incorrect behavior, check if there's a workaround.
306	       If no workaround, mark as high. If workaround exists, mark as medium.
307	       Cosmetic issues are always low priority.
308	       Finally, assign to the right team based on the component."
309	
310	Agent generates skill:
311	  skills/bug-triage/
312	  ├── skill.json          { name: "Bug Triage", domains: ["software", "qa"] }
313	  ├── triples.json        [ "crash is-a bug_category", "severity:critical is-a severity", ... ]
314	  ├── actions.json        [ { action: "categorize_bug", ... }, { action: "assess_severity", ... } ]
315	  ├── plans.json          [ { goal: "triage_bug", method: "sequential", steps: [...] } ]
316	  ├── rules.txt           (is_crash ?bug) => (severity ?bug critical)
317	  │                        (no_workaround ?bug) (incorrect_behavior ?bug) => (severity ?bug high)
318	  └── procedures.md       (original user text)
319	
320	Agent: "I've created the 'Bug Triage' skill with 8 domain concepts,
321	        3 action schemas, 1 plan template, and 4 inference rules.

1	# ADR 040 — Procedural Skills: From "What Is" to "How To Do"
2	
3	> Date: 2026-03-26
4	> Status: Proposed
5	> Phase: 30
6	> Depends on: Phase 26b (Candle LLM backend), Phase 15a (causal action schemas),
7	>             Phase 11 (HTN decomposition), Phase 16 (MCTS planning)
8	> Enhances: Phase 29b (skill exposure), Phase 27 (live training)
9	
10	## Context
11	
12	Akh-medu skills currently carry two types of knowledge:
13	
14	1. **Declarative** — triples in `triples.json` ("Pluto is-a DwarfPlanet")
15	2. **Inferential** — egg rewrite rules in `rules.txt` (`(causes ?x ?y) => (enables ?x ?y)`)
16	
17	This is powerful but incomplete. A human "skill" also includes **procedural
18	knowledge** — knowing *how to do things*: "To debug Rust: first read the error,
19	then trace the stack, then check the types..."
20	
21	Meanwhile, the engine already HAS procedural representation mechanisms that are
22	disconnected from the skill system:
23	
24	| System | Represents | Phase | In Skills? |
25	|---|---|---|---|
26	| HTN decomposition | Goal → ordered substeps | 11 | No |
27	| Causal action schemas | Action + preconditions + effects | 15a | No |
28	| MCTS plan templates | Scored multi-step strategies | 16 | No |
29	| Event calculus | "Doing X initiates Y, terminates Z" | 15b | No |
30	
31	Furthermore, egg rewrite rules require formal syntax expertise that most users
32	lack. The barrier to creating useful skills is too high.
33	
34	## Decision
35	
36	### 1. Extend the skill format with procedural knowledge files
37	
38	Add two new optional files to the skill directory:
39	
40	```
41	skills/{skill-id}/
42	├── skill.json         # Manifest (existing)
43	├── triples.json       # Declarative facts (existing)
44	├── rules.txt          # Inference rules (existing)
45	├── actions.json       # NEW: Causal action schemas
46	├── plans.json         # NEW: HTN decomposition templates
47	└── procedures.md      # NEW: Natural language source (for LLM re-generation)
48	```
49	
50	**actions.json** — Action schemas with preconditions and effects:
51	```json
52	[
53	  {
54	    "action": "read_entire_file",
55	    "preconditions": ["file_exists", "file_accessible"],
56	    "effects": {
57	      "initiates": ["context_understood"],
58	      "terminates": ["context_unknown"]
59	    },
60	    "description": "Read the entire file to understand its structure"
61	  }
62	]
63	```
64	
65	**plans.json** — HTN decomposition templates:
66	```json
67	[
68	  {
69	    "goal": "review_code",
70	    "method": "sequential",
71	    "steps": ["read_entire_file", "identify_bugs", "assess_severity",
72	              "suggest_fixes", "comment_style"],
73	    "preconditions": ["has_file_to_review"],
74	    "quality_gate": "all_steps_completed"
75	  }
76	]
77	```
78	
79	**procedures.md** — Natural language source of truth:
80	```markdown
81	# Code Review Procedure
82	
83	To review code:
84	1. First read the entire file to understand context
85	2. Check for common bugs (null derefs, off-by-one, resource leaks)
86	3. If you find a bug, note the line and severity
87	4. Suggest a fix with explanation
88	5. Only then comment on style issues
89	
90	Important: severity assessment before style — never block on formatting.
91	```
92	
93	### 2. Wire skill activation to CausalManager + HTN + MCTS
94	
95	When a skill transitions to Hot:
96	- `triples.json` → KG (existing)
97	- `rules.txt` → e-graph rule store (existing)
98	- `actions.json` → CausalManager.register_action_schema() (new wiring)
99	- `plans.json` → HTN decomposition templates + MCTS seed plans (new wiring)
100	
101	When deactivated:
102	- Action schemas deregistered from CausalManager
103	- HTN templates removed
104	- (Triples persist in KG as before — deactivate ≠ forget)
105	
106	### 3. LLM-assisted skill authoring via Candle
107	
108	The Candle LLM (Phase 26b) translates natural language procedures into the
109	structured skill format. Three authoring tiers:
110	
111	**Tier 1 — Casual user** (natural language only):
112	```
113	User: "I want to teach you how to review code. First read the file..."
114	  → LLM extracts domain concepts → triples.json
115	  → LLM extracts steps + ordering → plans.json
116	  → LLM extracts preconditions/effects → actions.json
117	  → LLM generates inference heuristics → rules.txt
118	  → Original text preserved → procedures.md
119	```
120	
121	**Tier 2 — Intermediate user** (edit generated files):
122	- LLM generates initial skill from natural language
123	- User edits JSON/rules to refine behavior
124	- Re-generation from procedures.md preserves manual edits via merge
125	
126	**Tier 3 — Expert user** (write directly):
127	- Author egg rules, action schemas, HTN plans by hand
128	- Full control, no LLM involvement
129	- Existing workflow, preserved as-is
130	
131	### 4. LLM-assisted rule refinement loop
132	
133	When the agent uses a skill's procedures and fails:
134	
135	1. Engine logs failure with provenance (which action failed, what precondition
136	   wasn't met, which rule didn't fire)
137	2. LLM analyzes the failure trace
138	3. LLM suggests:
139	   - New rules to handle the edge case
140	   - Modified action preconditions
141	   - Additional HTN decomposition paths (alternative methods)
142	4. Suggestions stored as pending updates (not auto-applied)
143	5. User reviews and approves via MCP/CLI/dashboard
144	6. Skill files updated, re-activated
145	
146	This is distinct from Phase 27 (neural weight training) — here we're refining
147	**symbolic** procedural knowledge, not neural parameters.
148	
149	### 5. Skill quality metrics
150	
151	Track per-skill:
152	- **Success rate**: % of plans using this skill's procedures that completed
153	- **Failure modes**: which actions fail most often, which preconditions are unmet
154	- **Rule hit rate**: which inference rules actually fire during reasoning
155	- **Coverage**: what fraction of the skill's triples are ever queried
156	- **Staleness**: time since last successful use
157	
158	Store as KG triples with `skill:quality_*` predicates. Surface in Phase 29b
159	dashboard.
160	
161	## Rejected Alternatives
162	
163	### Procedural knowledge as triples only
164	Attempted to encode "step 1 comes before step 2" as triples with ordering
165	predicates. Too verbose, hard to author, and loses the structured plan semantics
166	that HTN/MCTS need.
167	
168	### Separate "procedure" entity type
169	Considered adding a new SymbolKind for procedures. Rejected because action
170	schemas and HTN plans are already well-defined in the engine — we should reuse
171	them, not reinvent.
172	
173	### Auto-apply LLM rule suggestions
174	Too risky. LLM-generated rules can be subtly wrong. The human-in-the-loop
175	review step is essential for maintaining the engine's correctness guarantees.
176	
177	## Consequences
178	
179	- SkillManifest extended with `actions_file` and `plans_file` optional fields
180	- SkillManager.activate() wires to CausalManager + HTN + MCTS
181	- New module: `src/skills/author.rs` — LLM-assisted skill generation
182	- New module: `src/skills/refine.rs` — failure analysis + rule suggestion
183	- New module: `src/skills/quality.rs` — skill metrics tracking
184	- `procedures.md` becomes the user-friendly entry point for skill creation
185	- Phase 29b exposure gains "create skill from description" NLU intent
186	- Feature-gated: `skill-author` requires `candle-backend` (Phase 26b)
187	
188	## References
189	
190	- HTN planning: Phase 11, `src/agent/` (task decomposition)
191	- Causal action schemas: Phase 15a, `src/agent/causal.rs`
192	- MCTS planning: Phase 16, `src/agent/mcts.rs`
193	- Candle LLM backend: Phase 26b, ADR 037
194	- Skill exposure: Phase 29b, ADR 039
195

1	//! Skillpack manager: MoE-style modular expert loading.
2	//!
3	//! Skillpacks are loadable modules containing domain-specific knowledge
4	//! (triples), rewrite rules, and metadata. They follow a lifecycle:
5	//! Cold (on disk) → Warm (manifest parsed) → Hot (active in memory).
6	
7	pub mod manager;
8	
9	use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
10	
11	use crate::error::SkillResult;
12	
13	/// The lifecycle state of a skillpack.
14	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
15	pub enum SkillState {
16	    /// On disk, not loaded.
17	    Cold,
18	    /// Manifest loaded, ready to activate.
19	    Warm,
20	    /// Fully loaded and active in memory.
21	    Hot,
22	}
23	
24	impl std::fmt::Display for SkillState {
25	    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
26	        match self {
27	            Self::Cold => write!(f, "Cold"),
28	            Self::Warm => write!(f, "Warm"),
29	            Self::Hot => write!(f, "Hot"),
30	        }
31	    }
32	}
33	
34	/// Metadata describing a skillpack.
35	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
36	pub struct SkillManifest {
37	    /// Unique skillpack identifier.
38	    pub id: String,
39	    /// Human-readable name.
40	    pub name: String,
41	    /// Version string.
42	    pub version: String,
43	    /// Human-readable description.
44	    #[serde(default)]
45	    pub description: String,

1	# ADR 041 — Skill Intelligence: Self-Organizing Skill Ecosystem
2	
3	> Date: 2026-03-26
4	> Status: Proposed
5	> Phase: 31
6	> Depends on: Phase 30 (procedural skills), Phase 26d (neural bridge),
7	>             Phase 28 (n akh router)
8	> Enhances: Phase 27 (training data from skills), Phase 29b (skill exposure)
9	
10	## Context
11	
12	Phase 30 makes individual skills richer (procedural knowledge) and easier to
13	create (LLM-assisted authoring). Phase 31 addresses the ecosystem level:
14	how skills relate to each other, how they're discovered, how the engine
15	self-organizes its skill inventory.
16	
17	Currently:
18	- Skills are manually created and manually activated
19	- No dependency relationships between skills
20	- No way to discover that existing reasoning patterns should be packaged as skills
21	- No sharing mechanism beyond copying directories
22	- No awareness of which skills are relevant to a given query
23	- No cross-skill inference beyond shared KG triples
24	
25	## Decision
26	
27	### 1. Skill discovery from reasoning
28	
29	The agent already discovers facts during background learning (spreading
30	activation, sleep/dream phase, continuous learning). When it discovers a
31	cluster of related facts + inference patterns in a domain, it should
32	recognize this as a **latent skill** and offer to package it.
33	
34	**Trigger**: During background learning, if the consolidation phase identifies
35	N+ related triples (connected subgraph) with consistent provenance and high
36	usage, flag as skill candidate.
37	
38	**Process**:
39	1. Extract the connected subgraph of triples
40	2. Identify inference rules that fired within this subgraph
41	3. Identify action schemas that were used in this domain
42	4. LLM generates a skill name + description from the content
43	5. Store as `SkillCandidate` in KG (pending user approval)
44	6. User reviews and promotes to full skill
45	
46	### 2. Skill dependency graph
47	
48	Extend `SkillManifest` with:
49	```rust
50	pub depends: Vec<String>,           // Skill IDs that must be active first
51	pub conflicts: Vec<String>,         // Skill IDs that cannot be co-active
52	pub provides: Vec<String>,          // Capability tags this skill offers
53	pub requires: Vec<String>,          // Capability tags this skill needs
54	```
55	
56	**Activation**: Topological sort on dependency graph. Auto-activate
57	prerequisites. Reject activation if conflicts are detected.
58	
59	**Capability matching**: `provides`/`requires` enable loose coupling —
60	a skill says "I need spatial_reasoning" without naming a specific provider.
61	Multiple skills can provide the same capability (MoE selection).
62	
63	### 3. Neural skill embeddings
64	
65	Using Phase 26d's NeuralVsaBridge, create a **prototype HyperVec per skill**:
66	
67	- Bundle all of a skill's triple vectors into a single skill prototype
68	- Store in ItemMemory with a well-known `skill:prototype:{skill_id}` symbol
69	- Enable: "Which skill is most relevant to this query?" via similarity search
70	- Enable: "Which skills overlap?" via pairwise similarity
71	- Enable: "Which skill should I activate for this domain?" via n akh routing
72	
73	This is cheap — one extra HyperVec per skill, computed at activation time.
74	
75	### 4. Skill-aware routing (n akh integration)
76	
77	Extend Phase 28's `n akh` router with skill awareness:
78	
79	- Before routing a query, check similarity against skill prototypes
80	- If a relevant skill is Cold/Warm, auto-activate it (lazy loading)
81	- If multiple skills match, activate the one with highest quality score (Phase 30e)
82	- After query, if skill was auto-activated and isn't used again within
83	  cooldown period, auto-deactivate (memory conservation)
84	
85	This transforms skills from static, manually-managed knowledge packs into
86	**demand-loaded expertise modules**.
87	
88	### 5. Dynamic skill synthesis
89	
90	When the agent identifies a knowledge gap (directed curiosity, Phase 11j)
91	and can't find an existing skill:
92	
93	1. Agent recognizes gap: "I don't know how to reason about X"
94	2. Agent triggers bootstrap-style ingestion for domain X (web search, API)
95	3. Ingested knowledge is consolidated
96	4. LLM-assisted authoring (Phase 30c) packages the result as a new skill
97	5. New skill is activated and its quality tracked
98	
99	This closes the autonomy loop: the agent teaches itself by creating skills.
100	
101	### 6. Skill sharing protocol
102	
103	Skills are portable directories. A sharing protocol enables:
104	
105	**Export**: `akh skill export {name}` → produces a `.akhskill` archive
106	(tar.gz of the skill directory + integrity checksum)
107	
108	**Import**: `akh skill import {path}` → unpacks, validates manifest,
109	installs + activates
110	
111	**Registry** (future): A simple HTTP index where skills can be discovered
112	by domain tag, quality score, and compatibility version. Not a marketplace —
113	a FLOSS package registry like crates.io for skills.
114	
115	**Recipe integration**: Community recipes (Phase 14i) already reference
116	skillpacks by name. The sharing protocol provides the transport layer.
117	
118	### 7. Skill-to-skill inference
119	
120	Currently, triples from different skills coexist in the shared KG, enabling
121	implicit cross-skill inference via spreading activation. Make this explicit:
122	
123	**Bridge rules**: When two skills are co-active and share overlapping concepts
124	(detected via neural prototype similarity > threshold), generate bridge rules
125	that connect their ontologies.
126	
127	Example: "astronomy" skill has "star is-a celestial_body", "mythology" skill

23	## Library Usage Patterns
24	
25	### Error handling (miette + thiserror)
26	- All error enums derive `#[derive(Debug, Error, Diagnostic)]`
27	- Each variant has `#[diagnostic(code(...), help(...))]`
28	- Subsystem errors chain via `#[error(transparent)] #[diagnostic(transparent)]`
29	- Return `AkhResult<T>` (alias for `Result<T, AkhError>`) from public APIs
30	- Subsystem functions return their own result type (e.g., `VsaResult<T>`, `StoreResult<T>`)
31	
32	### HNSW (hnsw_rs + anndists)
33	- Import distances from `anndists::dist::DistHamming` (NOT `hnsw_rs::dist`)
34	- Hnsw requires lifetime: `Hnsw<'static, u32, DistHamming>`
35	- `insert()` takes `(&[T], usize)` tuple and uses `&self` (not `&mut self`)
36	- `search()` takes `(&[T], k, ef_search)` and returns `Vec<Neighbour>`
37	
38	### Oxigraph (SPARQL store)
39	- `Store::new()` for in-memory, `Store::open(path)` for persistent
40	- Triples use `Quad::new(subject, predicate, object, GraphNameRef::DefaultGraph)`
41	- SymbolId maps to IRI: `https://akh-medu.dev/sym/{id}`
42	- Query with `store.query("SELECT ...")` → `QueryResults::Solutions`
43	
44	### Petgraph (knowledge graph)
45	- Must `use petgraph::visit::EdgeRef` to access `.source()` and `.target()` on edges
46	- Use `DiGraph<SymbolId, EdgeData>` with separate `DashMap<SymbolId, NodeIndex>` index
47	
48	### Egg (e-graph reasoning)
49	- Define language with `define_language!` macro
50	- Create rules with `rewrite!` macro
51	- Run with `Runner::default().with_expr(&expr).run(&rules)`
52	- Extract best with `Extractor::new(&runner.egraph, AstSize)`
53	
54	### Redb (durable store)
55	- Define tables as const: `const TABLE: TableDefinition<&[u8], &[u8]> = TableDefinition::new("name")`
56	- Use `begin_write()` / `begin_read()` for transactions
57	- Drop table handles before calling `txn.commit()`
58	- When checking if remove() found something, extract the bool inside the scope
59	
60	### Edition 2024
61	- `unsafe fn` bodies are NOT implicitly unsafe — wrap each unsafe op in `unsafe {}`
62	- Use `edition = "2024"` in Cargo.toml
63	
64	### Agent module patterns
65	- Agent concepts (goals, memories, episodes) are **regular Entity symbols** with well-known relation predicates (prefixed `agent:`) — no new `SymbolKind` variants
66	- `AgentPredicates` holds 12 well-known relation SymbolIds resolved at agent init
67	- `AgentError::Engine` wraps `Box<AkhError>` to break the recursive type cycle; manual `From<AkhError>` impl handles boxing
68	- Memory consolidation stores `DerivationKind::AgentConsolidation` provenance; decisions store `DerivationKind::AgentDecision`
69	- Tools are compile-time trait impls (`impl Tool for X`) with runtime registration in `ToolRegistry`
70	- The OODA loop is synchronous — no async runtime

Perfect! Now I have enough information to provide a comprehensive overview. Let me compile the findings:

## Comprehensive Rust Workspace Overview

I've completed a thorough exploration of the workspace. Here's what I found:

---

### 1. **Overall Workspace Structure**

**Root Cargo.toml** (`/workspace/Cargo.toml`):
- Main package: **akh-medu** (v0.6.0)
- Edition: 2024 (Rust's latest experimental edition)
- Workspace members: `["."]` (main binary), `crates/seshat`
- Description: "Neuro-symbolic AI engine: VSA + knowledge graphs + symbolic reasoning"
- License: GPL-3.0-only

**Two main crates:**
1. **akh-medu (main)** — The neuro-symbolic engine with agent system, skills, and reasoning
2. **crates/seshat** (v0.1.0) — Shared corpus library with RAG + pgvector (PostgreSQL embeddings)

**Key directories:**
- `/workspace/src/` — Main engine and agent code (228KB main.rs!)
- `/workspace/crates/seshat/` — Archive/corpus service
- `/workspace/skills/` — Skillpacks (language, astronomy, geography, etc.)
- `/workspace/docs/ai/` — Architecture, phases, ADRs, and plans
- `/workspace/plugin-skills/` — Additional plugin-based skills
- `/workspace/agents/` — Agent manifests/configs

---

### 2. **Existing Skill System**

**Current Structure** (`SkillManifest` in `/workspace/src/skills/mod.rs`):
```rust
pub struct SkillManifest {
    pub id: String,                    // "language", "astronomy", etc.
    pub name: String,                  // Human-readable name
    pub version: String,               // Semver
    pub description: String,
    pub domains: Vec<String>,          // Domain tags
    pub weight_size_bytes: u64,        // Neural weights (0 if none)
    pub triples_file: Option<String>,  // Path to triples.json
    pub rules_file: Option<String>,    // Path to rules.txt (egg rewrite rules)
    pub cli_tools: Vec<String>,        // CLI tool manifests
    pub wasm_tools: Vec<String>,       // WASM modules
    pub tool_config: HashMap<String, String>, // Config for tools
}
```

**Skill Lifecycle** (Cold → Warm → Hot):
- **Cold**: On disk, not loaded
- **Warm**: Manifest parsed, ready to activate
- **Hot**: Fully loaded in memory (triples in KG, rules registered)

**Existing Skill Files** (`/workspace/skills/language/`):
- `skill.json` — Manifest (see example below)
- `triples.json` — Label-based triples in JSON format
- `rules.txt` — Rewrite rules in egg syntax

**Example Manifest** (`language/skill.json`):
```json
{
  "id": "language",
  "name": "Language Structure",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "description": "Parts of speech, sentence structure, and linguistic relations",
  "domains": ["language", "linguistics"],
  "weight_size_bytes": 0,
  "triples_file": "triples.json",
  "rules_file": "rules.txt"
}
```

**Example Triples** (first 10 of language/triples.json):
```json
[
  {"subject": "Noun", "predicate": "is-a", "object": "PartOfSpeech", "confidence": 1.0},
  {"subject": "Verb", "predicate": "is-a", "object": "PartOfSpeech", "confidence": 1.0},
  ...
]
```

**Example Rules** (language/rules.txt):
```
# Synonym symmetry: if X synonym-of Y, then Y synonym-of X
(synonym-of ?x ?y) => (synonym-of ?y ?x)
# Antonym symmetry: if X antonym-of Y, then Y antonym-of X
(antonym-of ?x ?y) => (antonym-of ?y ?x)
(inverse-of ?x ?y) => (inverse-of ?y ?x)
```

**Current SkillManager** (`/workspace/src/skills/manager.rs` — 572 lines):
- `discover()` — Scans skills directory for skill.json manifests
- `warm()` — Parses manifest (Cold→Warm)
- `activate()` — Loads triples into KG and rules (Warm→Hot)
- `deactivate()` — Marks as Warm, frees memory
- `skill_state()`, `list()`, `get_info()` — Queries
- `active_rules()` — Builds egg rewrite rules from Hot skills
- Memory budget enforcement (max_bytes per skill manager)

---

### 3. **Agent Module Structure** (`/workspace/src/agent/`)

**47 Rust files** covering:

**Core Agent**:
- `agent.rs` (116KB) — Main Agent struct, AgentConfig, AgentPredicates, OODA loop entry
- `mod.rs` — Module exports
- `error.rs` — AgentError types

**Reasoning Systems**:
- `ooda.rs` (72KB) — OODA loop (Observe-Orient-Decide-Act)
- `causal.rs` (40KB) — **Causal world model** (Phase 15a)
  - `CausalRelation` enum (Causes, Enables, Prevents, Inhibits)
  - `CausalPredicates` (well-known relation SymbolIds)
  - Action schemas with preconditions + effects
  - Transition prediction and outcome verification
- `mcts.rs` (25KB) — **Monte Carlo Tree Search planner** (Phase 16b)
  - `MctsConfig`, `MctsNode`, `ValueFunction`
  - UCT-based tree search with rollout evaluation
- `decomposition.rs` (41KB) — **HTN (Hierarchical Task Network)** (Phase 11)
  - Task decomposition, method registry, subtask ordering
- `event_calculus.rs` (39KB) — **Event Calculus** (Phase 15b)
  - Temporal reasoning, initiates/terminates fluents

**Planning & Execution**:
- `plan.rs` (37KB) — Plan structure, status tracking, monitoring
- `plan_monitor.rs` (12KB) — Plan execution monitoring
- `constraint_check.rs` (29KB) — Constraint satisfaction checking

**Memory & Learning**:
- `memory.rs` (35KB) — Working memory, consolidation, episodic storage
- `continuous_learning.rs` (18KB) — Background learning
- `library_learn.rs` (21KB) — Learning from examples

**Meta-cognition & Reflection**:
- `metacognition.rs` (42KB) — Competence models, failure analysis (Phase 11f)
- `reflect.rs` (28KB) — Reflection and adjustment

**Goals & Motivation**:
- `goal.rs` (29KB) — Goal structure, status, criteria
- `goal_generation.rs` (39KB) — Autonomous goal generation
- `drives.rs` (13KB) — Drive system (curiosity, competence)
- `priority_reasoning.rs` (28KB) — Goal prioritization

**Knowledge & Reasoning**:
- `epistemic.rs` (32KB) — Epistemic logic, belief states (Phase 19)
- `evidence.rs` (31KB) — Evidence theory, Dempster-Shafer (Phase 17)
- `credibility.rs` (18KB) — Source credibility assessment
- `counterfactual.rs` (19KB) — Counterfactual reasoning (Phase 15c)

**Communication & Interaction**:
- `chat.rs` (8KB) — Chat interface

**Social & Game-Theoretic**:

**Tools & Delegation**:

  - `local_claude.rs` — Delegate to local Claude subprocess

**Other**:
- `ach.rs` (16KB) — ACH (Analysis of Competing Hypotheses)
- `affect.rs` (23KB) — Affective system (Phase 23)
- `curiosity.rs` (16KB) — Directed curiosity (Phase 11j)
- `semantic_enrichment.rs` (28KB) — Semantic enrichment
- `chunking.rs` (38KB) — Procedural learning/chunking (Phase 11h)
- `sleep.rs` (26KB) — Sleep/consolidation cycles (Phase 11i)

- `contact_calendar.rs` (14KB) — Calendar integration

- `pim.rs` (82KB) — Personal Information Management

- `source_reliability.rs` (21KB) — Source reliability tracking
- `ambient_intelligence.rs` — Context awareness
- `tools/` — Tool implementations

---

### 4. **Procedural Skills (Phase 30) — Plans & ADRs**

**Plan**: `/workspace/docs/ai/plans/2026-03-26-phase30-procedural-skills.md`

**Status**: Planned (depends on Phase 26b, 15a, 11, 16)

**Proposed Extensions to SkillManifest**:
```rust
pub struct SkillManifest {
    // ... existing fields ...
    pub actions_file: Option<String>,    // Path to actions.json
    pub plans_file: Option<String>,      // Path to plans.json
    pub procedures_file: Option<String>, // Natural language source
}
```

**New Files to Add** (not yet implemented):

1. **actions.json** — Causal action schemas:
```json
[
  {
    "action": "read_entire_file",
    "description": "Read the entire file to understand its structure",
    "preconditions": ["file_exists", "file_accessible"],
    "effects": {
      "initiates": ["context_understood"],
      "terminates": ["context_unknown"]
    },

  }
]
```

2. **plans.json** — HTN decomposition templates:
```json

  {
    "goal": "review_code",

```

3. **procedures.md** — Natural language source (for LLM re-generation):
```markdown

```

**Phase 30 Sub-phases**:

1	//! Skillpack manager: MoE-style modular expert loading.
2	//!
3	//! Skillpacks are loadable modules containing domain-specific knowledge
4	//! (triples), rewrite rules, and metadata. They follow a lifecycle:
5	//! Cold (on disk) → Warm (manifest parsed) → Hot (active in memory).
6	
7	pub mod manager;
8	
9	use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
10	
11	use crate::error::SkillResult;
12	
13	/// The lifecycle state of a skillpack.
14	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
15	pub enum SkillState {
16	    /// On disk, not loaded.
17	    Cold,
18	    /// Manifest loaded, ready to activate.
19	    Warm,
20	    /// Fully loaded and active in memory.
21	    Hot,
22	}
23	
24	impl std::fmt::Display for SkillState {
25	    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
26	        match self {
27	            Self::Cold => write!(f, "Cold"),
28	            Self::Warm => write!(f, "Warm"),
29	            Self::Hot => write!(f, "Hot"),
30	        }
31	    }
32	}
33	
34	/// Metadata describing a skillpack.

36	pub struct SkillManifest {
37	    /// Unique skillpack identifier.
38	    pub id: String,

40	    pub name: String,

42	    pub version: String,

49	    #[serde(default)]

14	"I know how to review code", not just "I know facts about code review."

17	MCTS, event calculus) but they're disconnected from the skill system. And the
18	formal syntax for egg rules is a barrier for most users.

21	the LLM to make skill authoring accessible.

    pub success_rate: f32,           // Plans completed / plans attempted
    pub failure_modes: Vec<FailureMode>,
    pub rule_hit_rates: HashMap<String, f32>, // Rule name → % of inferences it participated in
    pub triple_coverage: f32,        // % of triples ever queried
    pub last_used: Option<u64>,      // Timestamp
    pub total_uses: u32,
    pub refinements_applied: u32,
    pub refinements_pending: u32,
}

pub struct FailureMode {
    pub action: String,
    pub failure_type: String,        // "precondition_unmet", "unexpected_effect", "timeout"
    pub count: u32,
    pub last_occurrence: u64,
}
```

**Storage**: Quality metrics stored as KG triples with `skill:quality_*`
predicates. Updated after each plan execution involving the skill.

**Staleness detection**: If a skill hasn't been used in N days and has low
coverage, suggest deactivation to free memory budget.

**MCP tools**: `skill_quality(skill_id)` returns the metrics.
**Dashboard**: Quality panel in Phase 29b skill browser.

## Estimated Effort

| Sub-phase | Lines | Complexity | Dependencies |
|---|---|---|---|
| 30a — Extended format | ~400 | Low | None (schema only) |
| 30b — Activation wiring | ~500 | Medium | Phase 15a, 11, 16 |
| 30c — LLM authoring | ~800 | High | Phase 26b (Candle) |
| 30d — Rule refinement | ~600 | High | Phase 26b, 30b |
| 30e — Quality metrics | ~300 | Low | 30b |
| **Total** | **~2,600** | | |

## New Dependencies

None — uses existing Candle (Phase 26b), serde for JSON, and existing engine
subsystems (CausalManager, HTN, MCTS).

## Feature Flags

```toml
[features]
skill-author = ["candle-backend"]  # LLM-assisted authoring (30c, 30d)
# 30a, 30b, 30e have no additional feature requirements
```

## Example: Teaching a Skill via Natural Language

```
User: "I want to teach you how to triage a bug report"

Agent: "I'll create a skill for that. Please describe the procedure."

User: "First categorize the bug: crash, incorrect behavior, or cosmetic.
       Then assess severity based on impact — crashes are always critical.
       For incorrect behavior, check if there's a workaround.
       If no workaround, mark as high. If workaround exists, mark as medium.
       Cosmetic issues are always low priority.
       Finally, assign to the right team based on the component."

Agent generates skill:
  skills/bug-triage/
  ├── skill.json          { name: "Bug Triage", domains: ["software", "qa"] }
  ├── triples.json        [ "crash is-a bug_category", "severity:critical is-a severity", ... ]
  ├── actions.json        [ { action: "categorize_bug", ... }, { action: "assess_severity", ... } ]
  ├── plans.json          [ { goal: "triage_bug", method: "sequential", steps: [...] } ]
  ├── rules.txt           (is_crash ?bug) => (severity ?bug critical)
  │                        (no_workaround ?bug) (incorrect_behavior ?bug) => (severity ?bug high)
  └── procedures.md       (original user text)

Agent: "I've created the 'Bug Triage' skill with 8 domain concepts,
        3 action schemas, 1 plan template, and 4 inference rules.
        Want me to activate it?"
```

## Relationship to Other Phases

- **Phase 26b** (Candle): Provides the LLM for authoring and refinement
- **Phase 27** (Burn training): Could train the LLM to be better at skill extraction
  over time (the skills it generates become training data)
- **Phase 28** (`n akh` router): Routes queries that match a skill's domain to the
  appropriate reasoning path
- **Phase 29b** (skill exposure): The user-facing controls for browsing, activating,
  and managing skills
- **Phase 31** (skill intelligence): Automatic skill discovery, dependency resolution,
  and ecosystem management

# ADR 040 — Procedural Skills: From "What Is" to "How To Do"

> Date: 2026-03-26
> Status: Proposed
> Phase: 30
> Depends on: Phase 26b (Candle LLM backend), Phase 15a (causal action schemas),
>             Phase 11 (HTN decomposition), Phase 16 (MCTS planning)
> Enhances: Phase 29b (skill exposure), Phase 27 (live training)

## Context

Akh-medu skills currently carry two types of knowledge:

1. **Declarative** — triples in `triples.json` ("Pluto is-a DwarfPlanet")
2. **Inferential** — egg rewrite rules in `rules.txt` (`(causes ?x ?y) => (enables ?x ?y)`)

This is powerful but incomplete. A human "skill" also includes **procedural
knowledge** — knowing *how to do things*: "To debug Rust: first read the error,
then trace the stack, then check the types..."

Meanwhile, the engine already HAS procedural representation mechanisms that are
disconnected from the skill system:

| System | Represents | Phase | In Skills? |
|---|---|---|---|
| HTN decomposition | Goal → ordered substeps | 11 | No |
| Causal action schemas | Action + preconditions + effects | 15a | No |
| MCTS plan templates | Scored multi-step strategies | 16 | No |
| Event calculus | "Doing X initiates Y, terminates Z" | 15b | No |

Furthermore, egg rewrite rules require formal syntax expertise that most users
lack. The barrier to creating useful skills is too high.

## Decision

### 1. Extend the skill format with procedural knowledge files

Add two new optional files to the skill directory:

```
skills/{skill-id}/
├── skill.json         # Manifest (existing)
├── triples.json       # Declarative facts (existing)
├── rules.txt          # Inference rules (existing)
├── actions.json       # NEW: Causal action schemas
├── plans.json         # NEW: HTN decomposition templates
└── procedures.md      # NEW: Natural language source (for LLM re-generation)
```

**actions.json** — Action schemas with preconditions and effects:
```json
[
  {
    "action": "read_entire_file",
    "preconditions": ["file_exists", "file_accessible"],
    "effects": {
      "initiates": ["context_understood"],
      "terminates": ["context_unknown"]
    },
    "description": "Read the entire file to understand its structure"
  }
]
```

**plans.json** — HTN decomposition templates:
```json
[
  {
    "goal": "review_code",
    "method": "sequential",
    "steps": ["read_entire_file", "identify_bugs", "assess_severity",
              "suggest_fixes", "comment_style"],
    "preconditions": ["has_file_to_review"],
    "quality_gate": "all_steps_completed"
  }
]
```

**procedures.md** — Natural language source of truth:
```markdown
# Code Review Procedure

To review code:
1. First read the entire file to understand context
2. Check for common bugs (null derefs, off-by-one, resource leaks)
3. If you find a bug, note the line and severity
4. Suggest a fix with explanation
5. Only then comment on style issues

Important: severity assessment before style — never block on formatting.
```

### 2. Wire skill activation to CausalManager + HTN + MCTS

When a skill transitions to Hot:
- `triples.json` → KG (existing)
- `rules.txt` → e-graph rule store (existing)
- `actions.json` → CausalManager.register_action_schema() (new wiring)
- `plans.json` → HTN decomposition templates + MCTS seed plans (new wiring)

When deactivated:
- Action schemas deregistered from CausalManager
- HTN templates removed
- (Triples persist in KG as before — deactivate ≠ forget)

### 3. LLM-assisted skill authoring via Candle

The Candle LLM (Phase 26b) translates natural language procedures into the
structured skill format. Three authoring tiers:

**Tier 1 — Casual user** (natural language only):
```
User: "I want to teach you how to review code. First read the file..."
  → LLM extracts domain concepts → triples.json
  → LLM extracts steps + ordering → plans.json
  → LLM extracts preconditions/effects → actions.json
  → LLM generates inference heuristics → rules.txt
  → Original text preserved → procedures.md
```

**Tier 2 — Intermediate user** (edit generated files):
- LLM generates initial skill from natural language
- User edits JSON/rules to refine behavior
- Re-generation from procedures.md preserves manual edits via merge

**Tier 3 — Expert user** (write directly):
- Author egg rules, action schemas, HTN plans by hand
- Full control, no LLM involvement
- Existing workflow, preserved as-is

### 4. LLM-assisted rule refinement loop

When the agent uses a skill's procedures and fails:

1. Engine logs failure with provenance (which action failed, what precondition
   wasn't met, which rule didn't fire)
2. LLM analyzes the failure trace
3. LLM suggests:
   - New rules to handle the edge case
   - Modified action preconditions
   - Additional HTN decomposition paths (alternative methods)
4. Suggestions stored as pending updates (not auto-applied)
5. User reviews and approves via MCP/CLI/dashboard
6. Skill files updated, re-activated

This is distinct from Phase 27 (neural weight training) — here we're refining
**symbolic** procedural knowledge, not neural parameters.

### 5. Skill quality metrics

Track per-skill:
- **Success rate**: % of plans using this skill's procedures that completed
- **Failure modes**: which actions fail most often, which preconditions are unmet
- **Rule hit rate**: which inference rules actually fire during reasoning
- **Coverage**: what fraction of the skill's triples are ever queried
- **Staleness**: time since last successful use

Store as KG triples with `skill:quality_*` predicates. Surface in Phase 29b
dashboard.

## Rejected Alternatives

### Procedural knowledge as triples only
Attempted to encode "step 1 comes before step 2" as triples with ordering
predicates. Too verbose, hard to author, and loses the structured plan semantics
that HTN/MCTS need.

### Separate "procedure" entity type
Considered adding a new SymbolKind for procedures. Rejected because action
schemas and HTN plans are already well-defined in the engine — we should reuse
them, not reinvent.

### Auto-apply LLM rule suggestions
Too risky. LLM-generated rules can be subtly wrong. The human-in-the-loop
review step is essential for maintaining the engine's correctness guarantees.

## Consequences

- SkillManifest extended with `actions_file` and `plans_file` optional fields
- SkillManager.activate() wires to CausalManager + HTN + MCTS
- New module: `src/skills/author.rs` — LLM-assisted skill generation
- New module: `src/skills/refine.rs` — failure analysis + rule suggestion
- New module: `src/skills/quality.rs` — skill metrics tracking
- `procedures.md` becomes the user-friendly entry point for skill creation
- Phase 29b exposure gains "create skill from description" NLU intent
- Feature-gated: `skill-author` requires `candle-backend` (Phase 26b)

## References

- HTN planning: Phase 11, `src/agent/` (task decomposition)
- Causal action schemas: Phase 15a, `src/agent/causal.rs`
- MCTS planning: Phase 16, `src/agent/mcts.rs`
- Candle LLM backend: Phase 26b, ADR 037
- Skill exposure: Phase 29b, ADR 039

2	//!
3	//! Explicit causal representation: cause-and-effect predicates, action schemas
4	//! with preconditions and effects, state transition prediction, and outcome
5	//! verification.  The causal model enables the agent to predict what will happen
6	//! before acting and to learn from the accuracy of its predictions.

34	    )]

1	//! HTN-style intelligent task decomposition.
2	//!
3	//! Replaces the simple comma/"and" splitting in `goal::generate_sub_goal_descriptions()`
4	//! with a method registry, VSA-based method selection, dependency DAGs,
5	//! and resource-rational scoring.
6	//!
7	//! # Architecture
8	//!
9	//! - **DecompositionMethod**: a reusable decomposition template with keyword hints,
10	//!   subtask templates, ordering constraints, and optional VSA semantic vector.
11	//! - **MethodRegistry**: stores methods and selects the best match for a goal
12	//!   via hybrid keyword + VSA scoring.
13	//! - **TaskTree**: a petgraph DAG of `TaskNode`s connected by `DependencyEdge`s.
14	//! - **decompose_goal_htn**: orchestrator that selects a method, instantiates it,
15	//!   builds the DAG, and returns a `DecompositionResult`.
16	
17	use miette::Diagnostic;
18	use petgraph::graph::{DiGraph, NodeIndex};
19	use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
20	use thiserror::Error;
21	
22	use crate::engine::Engine;
23	use crate::symbol::SymbolId;
24	use crate::vsa::HyperVec;
25	
26	use super::goal::{self, Goal};
27	use super::plan::PlanStep;
28	
29	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
30	// Error
31	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
32	
33	/// Errors during decomposition.
34	#[derive(Debug, Error, Diagnostic)]
35	pub enum DecompositionError {
36	    #[error("no applicable decomposition method for goal \"{goal_description}\"")]
37	    #[diagnostic(
38	        code(akh::agent::decomposition::no_method),
39	        help("The goal did not match any HTN method (score < 0.2). Falling back to comma-split decomposition.")
40	    )]
41	    NoApplicableMethod { goal_description: String },
42	
43	    #[error("dependency cycle detected in task tree for method \"{method_name}\"")]
44	    #[diagnostic(
45	        code(akh::agent::decomposition::cycle),
46	        help("The ordering constraints in the decomposition method form a cycle. Check the method's ordering pairs.")
47	    )]
48	    CycleDetected { method_name: String },
49	
50	    #[error("decomposition failed: {message}")]
51	    #[diagnostic(
52	        code(akh::agent::decomposition::failed),
53	        help("An internal error occurred during decomposition. Check the inner cause.")
54	    )]
55	    Failed { message: String },
56	}
57	
58	/// Convenience alias.
59	pub type DecompositionResult<T> = std::result::Result<T, DecompositionError>;
60	
61	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
62	// Strategy & Method
63	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
64	
65	/// High-level decomposition strategy.
66	#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
67	pub enum DecompositionStrategy {
68	    /// hypothesis → gather evidence → evaluate → conclude
69	    Research,
70	    /// define scope → build components → assemble → validate
71	    Construction,

input.content:
# Language Analysis Procedure

## Analysing a Sentence

To analyse the structure and meaning of a sentence:

1. **Parse sentence structure**: Identify the subject, predicate, verb phrase,
   and object. Note whether the sentence is declarative, interrogative, or
   imperative.

2. **Tag parts of speech**: For each word in the sentence, determine whether it
   is a noun, verb, adjective, adverb, pronoun, preposition, conjunction, or
   determiner.

3. **Resolve anaphora**: For any pronoun or definite noun phrase, find the noun
   or noun phrase it refers back to in the prior context.

## Quick Part-of-Speech Tagging

For a single word in context, identify its part of speech and note any
morphological features (tense, number, case).

## Understanding Discourse Relations

To understand how two clauses or sentences are related:

1. Parse each clause for its structural components.
2. Determine the discourse relation: contrast, cause-effect, elaboration,
   exemplification, temporal ordering, or condition.

## Important Principles

- Always consider context when tagging: "light" is an adjective in "light rain"
  but a noun in "turn off the light."
- Pronouns are resolved using the most recent, gender-congruent antecedent.
- Discourse relations are often signalled by connectives ("however", "because",
  "for example") but may be implicit.

content.text:
This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   Implement **Phase 30 — Procedural Skills** (work item `019db054-699b-7f72-bca2-589f5a6ba536`) for the `akh-medu` neuro-symbolic AI engine. This phase extends the skill system with procedural knowledge (actions, plans, HTN decomposition). The deliverables are:
   - **30a**: Extend `SkillManifest` with `actions_file`, `plans_file`, `procedures_file`; add types `SkillAction`, `SkillEffects`, `SkillPlan`, `PlanMethod`, `ConditionalStep`, `ActionDuration`
   - **30b**: Wire skill activation to load/store action schemas and plan templates in `SkillManager`
   - **30c**: Create `src/skills/author.rs` — LLM-assisted multi-pass skill authoring pipeline
   - **30d**: Create `src/skills/refine.rs` — failure analysis and rule refinement suggestion loop
   - **30e**: Create `src/skills/quality.rs` — per-skill quality metrics tracking
   - Add example `actions.json`/`plans.json`/`procedures.md` to existing skill packs
   - Build, test, lint (without committing; runner captures `git diff`)

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - **Rust workspace** with `akh-medu` main crate and `crates/seshat` sub-crate
   - **SkillManifest / SkillManager**: Cold→Warm→Hot lifecycle for loadable skill packs
   - **CausalManager** (`src/agent/causal.rs`): stores `ActionSchema` with preconditions/effects
   - **MethodRegistry** (`src/agent/decomposition.rs`): stores `DecompositionMethod` (HTN templates)
   - **MCTS** (`src/agent/mcts.rs`): Monte Carlo tree search planner
   - **LabelTriple**: `{subject, predicate, object, confidence}` for knowledge graph triples
   - **egg e-graph rewrite rules**: existing rule engine format `(lhs) => (rhs)`
   - **serde** with `#[serde(default)]` for backward-compatible manifest evolution
   - **`PlanMethod` tagged enum**: `#[serde(tag = "type", rename_all = "lowercase")]` → `{"type": "sequential"}`
   - **oxigraph → oxrocksdb-sys → bindgen → libclang**: complex C++ build dependency chain
   - **bindgen** needs `libclang` shared library at build time
   - **rustfmt** for code style enforcement

3. Files and Code Sections:

   - **`src/skills/mod.rs`** — Core skill types module. Extended to declare new sub-modules and add procedural types.
     ```rust
     pub mod author;
     pub mod manager;
     pub mod quality;
     pub mod refine;
     ```
     New fields on `SkillManifest`:
     ```rust
     #[serde(default)] pub actions_file: Option<String>,
     #[serde(default)] pub plans_file: Option<String>,
     #[serde(default)] pub procedures_file: Option<String>,
     ```
     New types added:
     ```rust
     pub struct SkillEffects {
         #[serde(default)] pub initiates: Vec<String>,
         #[serde(default)] pub terminates: Vec<String>,
     }
     
     #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize, Default)]
     #[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")]
     pub enum ActionDuration { #[default] Fast, Medium, Slow }
     
     pub struct SkillAction {
         pub action: String,
         #[serde(default)] pub description: String,
         #[serde(default)] pub preconditions: Vec<String>,
         #[serde(default)] pub effects: SkillEffects,
         #[serde(default)] pub estimated_duration: ActionDuration,
     }
     
     #[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, PartialEq)]
     #[serde(rename_all = "lowercase", tag = "type")]
     pub enum PlanMethod {
         Sequential,
         Parallel,
         Conditional { branches: Vec<ConditionalStep> },
     }
     
     pub struct SkillPlan {
         pub goal: String,
         #[serde(default)] pub method: PlanMethod,
         #[serde(default)] pub steps: Vec<String>,
         #[serde(default)] pub preconditions: Vec<String>,
         #[serde(default)] pub alternatives: Vec<String>,
         #[serde(default)] pub quality_gate: Option<String>,
     }
     ```
     Updated `LoadedSkill`:
     ```rust
     pub struct LoadedSkill {
         pub manifest: SkillManifest, pub state: SkillState,
         pub triple_count: usize, pub rule_count: usize, pub memory_bytes: usize,
         pub actions: Vec<SkillAction>,   // Phase 30
         pub plans: Vec<SkillPlan>,       // Phase 30
     }
     ```
     Updated `SkillInfo`:
     ```rust
     pub struct SkillInfo {
         // ... existing fields ...
         pub action_count: usize,  // Phase 30
         pub plan_count: usize,    // Phase 30
     }
     ```
     Updated `SkillActivation`:
     ```rust
     pub struct SkillActivation {
         pub skill_id: String, pub triples_loaded: usize,
         pub rules_loaded: usize, pub memory_bytes: usize,
         pub actions_loaded: usize,  // Phase 30
         pub plans_loaded: usize,    // Phase 30
     }
     ```

   - **`src/skills/manager.rs`** — Skill lifecycle manager. Extended `activate()` to load actions/plans.
     Key addition in `activate()`:
     ```rust
     // Load action schemas (actions.json)
     let actions_file = skill.manifest.actions_file.clone()
         .unwrap_or_else(|| "actions.json".into());
     let actions_path = skill_dir.join(&actions_file);
     let mut loaded_actions: Vec<SkillAction> = Vec::new();
     if actions_path.exists() {
         let content = std::fs::read_to_string(&actions_path)...?;
         loaded_actions = serde_json::from_str(&content)...?;
         memory_estimate += content.len();
     }
     // Similarly for plans.json → loaded_plans: Vec<SkillPlan>
     // Commit:
     skill.actions = loaded_actions;
     skill.plans = loaded_plans;
     ```
     In `deactivate()`:
     ```rust
     skill.actions.clear();
     skill.plans.clear();
     ```
     New public methods:
     ```rust
     pub fn actions(&self, skill_id: &str) -> Vec<SkillAction>
     pub fn plans(&self, skill_id: &str) -> Vec<SkillPlan>
     pub fn all_active_actions(&self) -> Vec<(String, SkillAction)>
     pub fn all_active_plans(&self) -> Vec<(String, SkillPlan)>
     ```
     New tests: `activate_loads_actions_and_plans`, `deactivate_clears_procedural_data`

   - **`src/skills/author.rs`** (NEW — Phase 30c) — LLM-assisted skill authoring
     ```rust
     pub struct SkillAuthor { llm_available: bool }
     
     pub struct AuthoredSkill {
         pub manifest: SkillManifest,
         pub triples: Vec<LabelTriple>,
         pub actions: Vec<SkillAction>,
         pub plans: Vec<SkillPlan>,
         pub rules: Vec<String>,
         pub source_text: String,
     }
     // Methods: write_to_disk(), validate()
     
     impl SkillAuthor {
         pub fn author_from_description(&self, id, name, description, hints) -> AuthorResult<AuthoredSkill>
         pub fn regenerate_from_procedures(&self, id, name, text, hints) -> AuthorResult<AuthoredSkill>
         pub fn build_action(action, description, preconditions, initiates, terminates) -> SkillAction
         pub fn build_sequential_plan(goal, steps, preconditions) -> SkillPlan
     }
     ```
     Validation checks: duplicate action names, plan steps reference known actions.
     When LLM is unavailable, returns a stub skill with empty procedural content and logs a warning.

   - **`src/skills/refine.rs`** (NEW — Phase 30d) — Rule refinement loop
     ```rust
     pub enum FailureType {
         PreconditionUnmet, UnexpectedEffect, Timeout, UnknownAction, GoalNotAchieved, Other(String)
     }
     pub struct FailureContext { skill_id, goal, failed_action, failure_type, world_state_fluents,
                                 unmet_preconditions, missing_effects, timestamp, provenance_id }
     #[serde(tag = "kind", rename_all = "snake_case")]
     pub enum RefinementKind {
         NewRule { lhs, rhs }, ModifiedPrecondition { action, add, remove },
         ModifiedEffect { action, add_initiates, remove_initiates, add_terminates, remove_terminates },
         AlternativePlan { goal, new_plan }, NewAction { action }, MissingTriple { triple },
     }
     pub struct RefinementSuggestion { id, skill_id, refinement, rationale, confidence,
                                       source_failure_action, created_at, reviewed, accepted }
     pub struct PendingRefinements { suggestions: HashMap<String, Vec<RefinementSuggestion>> }
     // Methods: add(), pending_for(), all(), accept(), reject(), clear_skill(), pending_count()
     pub struct SkillRefiner { llm_available: bool }
     // Methods: analyze_failure(), analyze_batch()
     ```
     Heuristic rules:
     - `PreconditionUnmet` → suggest removing unmet preconditions + new inference rule
     - `UnexpectedEffect` → suggest updating effects list
     - `UnknownAction` → suggest adding stub action
     - `GoalNotAchieved` → suggest alternative plan

   - **`src/skills/quality.rs`** (NEW — Phase 30e) — Per-skill quality metrics
     ```rust
     pub struct SkillQuality {
         pub skill_id: String, pub success_rate: f32, pub total_executions: u32,
         pub successful_executions: u32, pub failure_modes: Vec<FailureMode>,
         pub rule_hit_rates: HashMap<String, f32>, pub total_inference_passes: u64,
         pub triple_coverage: f32, pub triples_queried: usize, pub triples_total: usize,
         pub last_used: Option<u64>, pub refinements_pending: u32, pub refinements_applied: u32,
     }
     // Mutation: record_success(), record_failure(), record_rule_hit(), record_rule_miss(),
     //           record_triple_query(), set_refinements_pending(), record_refinement_applied()
     // Derived: top_failure_mode(), low_hit_rate_rules()
     
     pub struct StalenessConfig { stale_days: 30, min_coverage: 0.1, min_success_rate: 0.5 }
     pub struct QualityRegistry { records: HashMap<String, SkillQuality>, config: StalenessConfig }
     // Methods: ensure(), get(), get_mut(), stale_skills(), underperforming_skills(), all(), remove()
     ```

   - **`skills/language/skill.json`** — Updated version to 1.1.0, added procedural file declarations
   - **`skills/language/actions.json`** (NEW) — 4 action schemas (identify_part_of_speech, parse_sentence_structure, detect_discourse_relation, resolve_anaphora)
   - **`skills/language/plans.json`** (NEW) — 3 plan templates (analyse_sentence, quick_pos_tag, understand_discourse)
   - **`skills/language/procedures.md`** (NEW) — Natural language procedures source
   - **`skills/common_sense/skill.json`** — Updated version to 1.1.0, added procedural file declarations
   - **`skills/common_sense/actions.json`** (NEW) — 3 action schemas
   - **`skills/common_sense/plans.json`** (NEW) — 2 plan templates

4. Errors and Fixes:
   - **`libclang` not found for `bindgen`**: The project uses `oxigraph` → `oxrocksdb-sys` → `bindgen` which requires `libclang` at build time. No root access to install via `apt-get`.
     - Fix attempt: Downloaded individual `.deb` packages from `http://deb.debian.org/debian` and extracted them to `/tmp/libclang_extract/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/`: `libclang1-14`, `libllvm14`, `libedit2`, `libz3-4`, `libxml2`, `libbsd0`, `libicu72`. All `ldd` dependencies for `libclang-14.so.14.0.6` resolved after this.
     - Set `LIBCLANG_PATH=/tmp/libclang_extract/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu` and `LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/tmp/libclang_extract/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu` when running cargo.
     - **Status**: Still failing — latest build output shows `thread 'main' panicked at .../oxrocksdb-sys-0.5.5/build.rs:38:10` (line 38 is the `bindgen_rocksdb_api` function's `.generate().unwrap()`). The `bindings.rs` file has not yet been generated in any of the build output directories.
   - **`SkillInfo` missing `action_count`/`plan_count` fields**: Added them when extending the struct; `main.rs` only reads from `SkillInfo` (doesn't construct it), so no changes needed there.
   - **rustfmt formatting issues**: `rustfmt --check` revealed formatting differences in `author.rs`, `refine.rs`, `quality.rs`, `manager.rs`. Fixed by running `rustfmt` on all modified skill files.

5. Problem Solving:
   - **Phase 30a/30b**: Fully implemented. `SkillManifest` now carries optional `actions_file`/`plans_file`/`procedures_file` (all `#[serde(default)]` for backward compatibility). `SkillManager::activate()` loads both files and stores parsed data in `LoadedSkill`. New accessor methods expose the loaded procedural data to callers (e.g., agent code that would wire to `CausalManager`/`MethodRegistry`).

   - **Phase 30d**: `SkillRefiner` implemented with heuristic suggestions as fallback for LLM. `PendingRefinements` manages in-memory store of suggestions with accept/reject workflow.

1	# Phase 30 — Procedural Skills
2	
3	> Date: 2026-03-26
4	> Status: Planned
5	> Phase: 30
6	> Depends on: Phase 26b (Candle LLM), Phase 15a (causal schemas), Phase 11 (HTN)
7	> Enhances: Phase 29b (skill exposure), Phase 31 (skill intelligence)
8	> ADR: [040-procedural-skills](../decisions/040-procedural-skills.md)
9	
10	## Motivation
11	
12	Akh-medu skills currently carry facts and inference rules but no procedural
13	knowledge — "how to do things." A human expects a "skill" to mean capability:
14	"I know how to review code", not just "I know facts about code review."
15	
16	The engine already has procedural representation mechanisms (HTN, causal schemas,
17	MCTS, event calculus) but they're disconnected from the skill system. And the
18	formal syntax for egg rules is a barrier for most users.
19	
20	This phase bridges both gaps: extend skills with procedural knowledge, and use
21	the LLM to make skill authoring accessible.
22	
23	## Sub-phases
24	
25	### 30a — Extended Skill Format (~400 lines)
26	
27	Add `actions.json` and `plans.json` to the skill directory structure.
28	
29	**Extend SkillManifest**:
30	```rust
31	pub struct SkillManifest {
32	    // ... existing fields ...
33	    pub actions_file: Option<String>,    // Path to actions.json (default: "actions.json")
34	    pub plans_file: Option<String>,      // Path to plans.json (default: "plans.json")
35	    pub procedures_file: Option<String>, // Path to procedures.md (source of truth)
36	}
37	```
38	
39	**ActionSchema** (reuse existing `src/agent/causal.rs` types):
40	```rust
41	// actions.json is deserialized into Vec<SkillAction>
42	pub struct SkillAction {
43	    pub action: String,              // Action name (becomes a SymbolId)
44	    pub description: String,         // Human-readable purpose
45	    pub preconditions: Vec<String>,  // Fluent names that must hold
46	    pub effects: SkillEffects,
47	    pub estimated_duration: Option<String>, // "fast", "medium", "slow"
48	}
49	
50	pub struct SkillEffects {
51	    pub initiates: Vec<String>,      // Fluents this action starts
52	    pub terminates: Vec<String>,     // Fluents this action ends
53	}
54	```
55	
56	**PlanTemplate** (maps to HTN decomposition):
57	```rust
58	// plans.json is deserialized into Vec<SkillPlan>
59	pub struct SkillPlan {
60	    pub goal: String,                // Goal name (becomes a SymbolId)
61	    pub method: PlanMethod,          // How steps are organized
62	    pub steps: Vec<String>,          // Action names (references to actions.json)
63	    pub preconditions: Vec<String>,  // When this plan is applicable
64	    pub alternatives: Vec<String>,   // Other plan names that achieve the same goal
65	}
66	
67	pub enum PlanMethod {
68	    Sequential,                      // Steps must execute in order
69	    Parallel,                        // Steps can execute concurrently
70	    Conditional(Vec<ConditionalStep>), // Steps depend on runtime conditions
71	}
72	
73	pub struct ConditionalStep {
74	    pub condition: String,           // Fluent to check
75	    pub then_step: String,           // Action if true
76	    pub else_step: Option<String>,   // Action if false
77	}
78	```
79	
80	**Modify**: `src/skills/mod.rs`, `src/skills/manager.rs`
81	
82	### 30b — Activation Wiring (~500 lines)
83	
84	Wire skill activation to the procedural reasoning systems.
85	
86	**On skill activate (Hot)**:
87	```rust
88	// In SkillManager::activate() — after triples + rules:
89	
90	// 1. Load action schemas → CausalManager
91	if let Some(actions_path) = manifest.actions_file {
92	    let actions: Vec<SkillAction> = load_json(&skill_dir.join(actions_path))?;
93	    for action in &actions {
94	        let schema = action.to_causal_schema(engine)?; // resolve labels to SymbolIds
95	        engine.causal_manager().register_action_schema(schema)?;
96	    }
97	}
98	
99	// 2. Load plan templates → HTN decomposer + MCTS seed
100	if let Some(plans_path) = manifest.plans_file {
101	    let plans: Vec<SkillPlan> = load_json(&skill_dir.join(plans_path))?;
102	    for plan in &plans {
103	        let htn_rule = plan.to_htn_rule(engine)?;
104	        engine.htn_decomposer().register_rule(htn_rule)?;
105	
106	        // Seed MCTS with known-good plans for warm-start
107	        let mcts_seed = plan.to_mcts_seed(engine)?;
108	        engine.mcts_planner().add_seed(mcts_seed)?;
109	    }
110	}
111	```
112	
113	**On skill deactivate (Warm)**:
114	- Deregister action schemas from CausalManager (by skill_id tag)
115	- Remove HTN rules from decomposer (by skill_id tag)
116	- Remove MCTS seeds (by skill_id tag)
117	
118	**Provenance**: All skill-originated actions/plans get
119	`DerivationKind::SkillProcedure { skill_id, source_file }` provenance.
120	
121	**Modify**: `src/skills/manager.rs`, `src/agent/causal.rs`, `src/agent/ooda.rs`
122	
123	### 30c — LLM-Assisted Skill Authoring (~800 lines)
124	
125	**New module**: `src/skills/author.rs`
126	
127	The authoring pipeline takes natural language and produces a complete skill:
128	
129	```rust
130	pub struct SkillAuthor {
131	    llm: Arc<CandleBackend>,     // Phase 26b
132	    grammar: Arc<ConcreteGrammar>,
133	    engine: Arc<Engine>,
134	}
135	
136	pub struct AuthoredSkill {
137	    pub manifest: SkillManifest,
138	    pub triples: Vec<LabelTriple>,
139	    pub actions: Vec<SkillAction>,
140	    pub plans: Vec<SkillPlan>,
141	    pub rules: Vec<String>,          // egg rule strings
142	    pub source_text: String,         // Original natural language
143	}
144	
145	impl SkillAuthor {
146	    /// Generate a complete skill from natural language description
147	    pub fn author_from_description(
148	        &self,
149	        name: &str,
150	        description: &str,
151	        domains: &[String],
152	    ) -> SkillResult<AuthoredSkill>;
153	
154	    /// Re-generate structured files from updated procedures.md
155	    pub fn regenerate_from_procedures(
156	        &self,
157	        skill_id: &str,
158	        procedures_text: &str,
159	    ) -> SkillResult<AuthoredSkill>;
160	}
161	```
162	
163	**LLM prompt strategy** (structured extraction):
164	
165	The LLM receives a system prompt with:
166	1. The skill format specification (JSON schemas for actions/plans)
167	2. Examples of well-formed skills
168	3. The user's natural language description
169	
170	Output is constrained to produce valid JSON sections via the LogitsProcessor
171	(Phase 26b) or brace-depth tracking.
172	
173	**Multi-pass extraction**:
174	1. **Concept pass**: Extract domain entities and relationships → triples
175	2. **Action pass**: Extract steps with preconditions/effects → actions
176	3. **Plan pass**: Extract goal decomposition and ordering → plans
177	4. **Rule pass**: Extract heuristics and inference patterns → rules
178	5. **Validation pass**: Check internal consistency (all action refs in plans
179	   exist, all preconditions reference known fluents)
180	
181	Each pass uses a focused prompt to avoid overwhelming the small LLM.
182	For Qwen2.5-1.5B, this means 5 short inference calls rather than 1 long one.
183	
184	**NLU integration**:
185	- New dialogue act: `SkillTeach { name, description }`
186	- Grammar patterns: "teach me to...", "learn how to...", "I want to show you how..."
187	- ChatProcessor routes to SkillAuthor when detected
188	
189	### 30d — Rule Refinement Loop (~600 lines)
190	
191	**New module**: `src/skills/refine.rs`
192	
193	When the agent executes a skill's procedures and encounters problems:
194	
195	```rust
196	pub struct SkillRefiner {
197	    llm: Arc<CandleBackend>,
198	    engine: Arc<Engine>,
199	}
200	
201	pub struct RefinementSuggestion {
202	    pub skill_id: String,
203	    pub kind: RefinementKind,
204	    pub description: String,         // Human-readable explanation
205	    pub confidence: f32,
206	    pub source_failure: ProvenanceId, // What provoked this suggestion
207	}
208	
209	pub enum RefinementKind {
210	    NewRule { lhs: String, rhs: String },
211	    ModifiedPrecondition { action: String, add: Vec<String>, remove: Vec<String> },
212	    AlternativePlan { goal: String, new_method: SkillPlan },
213	    NewAction { action: SkillAction },
214	    TripleMissing { triple: LabelTriple },
215	}
216	```
217	
218	**Failure analysis pipeline**:
219	1. Agent executes plan from skill, action fails (precondition unmet or
220	   unexpected outcome)
221	2. Engine records failure with full provenance chain
222	3. Refiner queries: "What state was expected? What state was actual?
223	   What inference path was taken?"
224	4. LLM receives the failure context + skill's procedures.md
225	5. LLM generates RefinementSuggestions
226	6. Suggestions stored as pending (KG triples with `skill:pending_refinement`
227	   predicate)
228	7. User reviews via MCP/CLI/dashboard: approve, reject, or modify
229	
230	**Idle task integration**:
231	- New daemon idle task: `refine_skills` (runs every 30 min)
232	- Scans recent failures involving skill procedures
233	- Batches failure contexts for efficient LLM processing
234	- Accumulates suggestions without blocking
235	
236	### 30e — Skill Quality Metrics (~300 lines)
237	
238	**New module**: `src/skills/quality.rs`
239	
240	Track per-skill effectiveness:
241	
242	```rust
243	pub struct SkillQuality {
244	    pub skill_id: String,
245	    pub success_rate: f32,           // Plans completed / plans attempted
246	    pub failure_modes: Vec<FailureMode>,
247	    pub rule_hit_rates: HashMap<String, f32>, // Rule name → % of inferences it participated in
248	    pub triple_coverage: f32,        // % of triples ever queried
249	    pub last_used: Option<u64>,      // Timestamp
250	    pub total_uses: u32,
251	    pub refinements_applied: u32,
252	    pub refinements_pending: u32,
253	}
254	
255	pub struct FailureMode {
256	    pub action: String,
257	    pub failure_type: String,        // "precondition_unmet", "unexpected_effect", "timeout"
258	    pub count: u32,
259	    pub last_occurrence: u64,
260	}
261	```
262	
263	**Storage**: Quality metrics stored as KG triples with `skill:quality_*`
264	predicates. Updated after each plan execution involving the skill.
265	
266	**Staleness detection**: If a skill hasn't been used in N days and has low
267	coverage, suggest deactivation to free memory budget.
268	
269	**MCP tools**: `skill_quality(skill_id)` returns the metrics.
270	**Dashboard**: Quality panel in Phase 29b skill browser.
271	
272	## Estimated Effort
273

277	| 30b — Activation wiring | ~500 | Medium | Phase 15a, 11, 16 |
278	| 30c — LLM authoring | ~800 | High | Phase 26b (Candle) |
279	| 30d — Rule refinement | ~600 | High | Phase 26b, 30b |

287	
288	## Feature Flags
289	
290	```toml
291	[features]
292	skill-author = ["candle-backend"]  # LLM-assisted authoring (30c, 30d)
293	# 30a, 30b, 30e have no additional feature requirements
294	```
295	
296	## Example: Teaching a Skill via Natural Language
297	
298	```
299	User: "I want to teach you how to triage a bug report"
300	
301	Agent: "I'll create a skill for that. Please describe the procedure."
302	
303	User: "First categorize the bug: crash, incorrect behavior, or cosmetic.
304	       Then assess severity based on impact — crashes are always critical.
305	       For incorrect behavior, check if there's a workaround.
306	       If no workaround, mark as high. If workaround exists, mark as medium.
307	       Cosmetic issues are always low priority.
308	       Finally, assign to the right team based on the component."
309	
310	Agent generates skill:
311	  skills/bug-triage/
312	  ├── skill.json          { name: "Bug Triage", domains: ["software", "qa"] }
313	  ├── triples.json        [ "crash is-a bug_category", "severity:critical is-a severity", ... ]
314	  ├── actions.json        [ { action: "categorize_bug", ... }, { action: "assess_severity", ... } ]
315	  ├── plans.json          [ { goal: "triage_bug", method: "sequential", steps: [...] } ]
316	  ├── rules.txt           (is_crash ?bug) => (severity ?bug critical)
317	  │                        (no_workaround ?bug) (incorrect_behavior ?bug) => (severity ?bug high)
318	  └── procedures.md       (original user text)
319	
320	Agent: "I've created the 'Bug Triage' skill with 8 domain concepts,
321	        3 action schemas, 1 plan template, and 4 inference rules.
322	        Want me to activate it?"
323	```
